analysis.title: "The Nightmare Scenario": MOVE Creator Bassman Warns The 20Y At 6% Could Unleash "Convexity Vortex"
key_insights: Harley Bassman argues the roughly $200B CBOT Treasury bond future has become significantly negatively convex for the first time since early 2007. He says this has likely contributed to the recent rapid rise in rates as bond traders try to reduce risk at the same time.

With the 20Y yield near 5.68% (contract at 102.25), the cheapest-to-deliver (CTD) bond has shifted to a 13.24 duration bond, about 20% longer than a few weeks ago. Portfolio managers holding a fixed risk level must shed or hedge about 20% of their fixed-income risk.

The nightmare scenario is the 20Y crossing 6.0% with the CTD extending to a duration above 17. Bassman estimates such a delivery switch equals the Treasury auctioning $110B of 20Y bonds over four months.

Mechanism: conversion factors come from a fixed two-factor matrix of coupon and time to maturity, regardless of yield level. The contract is stipulated as a 6% coupon bond. Below 6% on the 20Y the CTD is one of the shortest bonds in the basket, and above 6% it is one of the longest.

The delivery option stayed worth little while the contract traded above 110. Below that level it became live, so the long side does not know its interest-rate exposure and the contract is negatively convex.

CTD progression: early July with the 20Y near 5% and the contract at 111.26, CTD was T 4¾ 11/15/43 (duration 11.03). Near 106.78 it moved to T 4¾ 02/15/45 (11.63). At 102.25 it is T 2½ 02/15/45 (13.24).
The last 70bp of selloff (4.98% to 5.68%) added 2.2 years of duration. The next 35bp would add 3.6 years as the CTD moves to T 1⅝ 11/15/50, and another 35bp reaches 17.47 years via T 1⅜ 08/15/50.
Negative convexity is pro-cyclical: as prices fall the CTD lengthens, hedge selling pushes rates higher, and another CTD shift follows. Managers must buy as prices rise and sell as they fall.

CFTC and Bloomberg data point to forced selling already underway. Money managers cut their ultra-long bond futures longs by about $27M per basis point of risk in the two weeks to Oct 6 (about $38B of 10Y-note equivalent). Asset-manager net long is the smallest since September 2025, and ultra-long open interest fell seven straight sessions.
Goldman's futures strategists saw institutional shorts in the long bond rise sharply since mid-September. Goldman's real-money duration exposure gauge is at -2, an increasing underweight.

Goldman rates strategist William Marshall argues convexity amplified the move but should be a much smaller factor in further selloffs. Goldman estimates about $60B of 10Y-equivalent MBS hedging since early September plus $10-15B from CTD switches. It says index-level MBS convexity is about zero and CTD-switch risk is no longer clearly asymmetric to higher yields, and it is more bullish on duration.
The author disputes Goldman, noting Bassman's grid is asymmetric: a 35bp rally shortens duration by 1.6 years to 11.63, while a 35bp selloff lengthens it by 3.6 years to 16.84.

Basis-trade risk: Bassman warns hedge-fund basis traders may close out positions by selling Treasuries. The basis trade was about $830B as of September 2025 versus $430B before March 2020. The author says an exit would hit cash Treasuries as futures cheapen versus cash.

Bassman's macro concern is trust in fiscal policy. A 10Y TIPS real rate of 2.90% is the market 'waving the white flag' on a fiscal problem. He proposes a medium-term deficit path (deficit at 6.2%) including lifting the $184,500 Social Security tax cap, raising the retirement age, means testing, and ending the estate-tax step-up basis.

Last month's 20Y auction priced at 5.420%, the highest yield since the tenor returned in 2020. It tailed by 2.0bps and Indirects fell to a record low 52.5%. Citi expects Treasury to trim 20Y auctions by $3B each next month.

The 20Y closed at 5.65% on Friday after peaking at 5.71% on Oct 7. The author sees a cushion of only 30-35bp before 6% and sides with Bassman over Goldman. The last 20Y breach of 6% was November 1999.

risk_factors: 20Y yield crossing 6.0% could force the CTD to extend to duration above 17, creating about $110B of 20Y-equivalent supply over four months.
Pro-cyclical negative convexity feedback loop in Treasury futures: lower prices lead to a longer CTD, more hedge selling, and then another CTD shift.
Hedge-fund basis traders unwinding by selling cash Treasuries alongside asset-manager futures selling.
Weak demand for long-end auctions, with the September 20Y auction at a record-low Indirects share.

The author also cites a Treasury that can't count on Japan and a European bond market going 'full PIIGS' as additional risks.

vol_and_positioning: Treasury bond futures have turned negatively convex: the contract falls faster and rises slower, which forces risk-constant managers to sell into declines and buy into rallies.

CFTC data show asset managers' ultra-long bond futures net long at the smallest since September 2025. Money managers cut about $27M per basis point of risk in the two weeks to Oct 6, and ultra-long open interest fell about $20M per basis point over seven sessions.
Goldman reports institutional shorts in the long bond rose sharply since mid-September, and its real-money duration gauge is at -2.

The basis trade, about $830B as of September 2025, is vulnerable to higher bond volatility. White's line in the sand cited is 5.25%-5.50% on yields, above which stocks and bonds fall together. The 10Y has spent most of the past two weeks above 5.25%.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman says negative convexity should be a much smaller factor in further selloffs. It puts index-level MBS convexity near zero, says CTD-switch risk is no longer clearly asymmetric to higher yields, and sees cheap valuations and underweight positioning supporting duration.
tension_points.bear_case: Bassman and the author say CTD duration rises by more in the next 35bp (3.6 years) than in the last 70bp (2.2 years). CFTC data show asset managers already selling, and basis traders could add more selling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 20Y crossing 6.0% with the CTD extending to duration above 17 would invalidate Goldman's constructive duration view.

theme_stances.key_argument: The CTD shift makes the bond future negatively convex, so hedging flows amplify selloffs as the 20Y approaches 6%.
theme_stances.evidence: One should consider 6% on the UST 20yr rate to be a bubbling Convexity Vortex
